Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Business outlets are overwhelmingly focused on the Nov. 3 US midterm elections and their market implications, with reporters framing it as a referendum on Trump and gaming out a likely 'blue wave' that could reshape AI, health-care and antitrust policy. A second major thread is the cooling AI trade—tech selloffs, Anthropic's IPO financials, and credit-rating warnings on Meta—alongside Saudi Aramco earnings and fallout from the record Binance crypto hack.

stories.headline: Wall Street and business leaders brace for a possible Democratic 'blue wave'
stories.summary: NYT reports that business executives and investors are preparing for a Democratic sweep in the midterms and weighing the fallout for data-center, cryptocurrency and other policy areas; FT, Politico and Axios all frame the vote as a high-stakes referendum on Trump with prediction markets (Kalshi, Polymarket) showing roughly 74-75% odds of a Democratic Senate takeover.

stories.headline: AI trade wobbles as Anthropic IPO filing shows slowing growth and Meta's credit outlook turns negative
stories.summary: Fortune reports that Anthropic's amended S-1 showed third-quarter revenue reaching $17 billion but growth slowing sharply and the company swinging back to an operating loss, while S&P separately cut its outlook on Meta to negative over AI capex concerns; WSJ's markets coverage noted tech stocks and chipmakers rebounding on election day after a rough October for the AI trade.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco profit surges despite pipeline and refinery attacks
stories.summary: State-run Saudi Aramco posted a 9 percent jump in third-quarter profit, which the company attributed to higher crude volumes and refined-product prices even as its facilities absorbed damaging attacks.

stories.headline: Binance hackers used fake job interviews and fabricated social media profiles in record $6.3bn heist
stories.summary: FT reports that Binance's internal investigation into the biggest crypto theft in history found human error played a major role, as fake interviews and social profiles were used to breach the exchange; North Korea has swiftly and unusually denied involvement despite US agencies blaming Pyongyang.

stories.headline: Disney plans several thousand layoffs, pushes managers to cut costs up to 20%
stories.summary: CNBC reports Disney expects to lay off several thousand employees in its latest cost-cutting round and is asking some managers to trim budgets by as much as a fifth.

stories.headline: Elite law firm Weil Gotshal collapses after 95 years following failed merger talks
stories.summary: Bloomberg's legal coverage detailed how Weil Gotshal & Manges collapsed this week after merger talks fell through, a stunning downfall for one of Wall Street's most storied law firms; Fortune separately noted the episode highlights the risk of firms built around star talent.

stories.headline: Billionaire Mark Walter explores sale of stakes in Cadillac F1 and $71bn insurer Delaware Life
stories.summary: FT reports Mark Walter has explored selling his Delaware Life insurance business as part of a broader restructuring of his TWG Global holding company, while WSJ separately reported Walter is in talks to sell his Cadillac F1 stake to the owners of the Red Sox and Liverpool at a valuation above $3 billion.

stories.headline: US home prices fall for the first time in three years
stories.summary: The Washington Post reports national home prices are declining for the first time in three years even as some markets like San Francisco continue to rise sharply, underscoring a bifurcated housing picture as the Economist separately flagged that several gauges of American renters' financial health are flashing red.

Business.gaps: The Information and Forbes produced no distinct midterm or markets coverage found in this search window; Business Insider's recent output could not be verified via search and no relevant feed items were provided for it.

US politics.overview: US political outlets are almost entirely consumed by Election Day 2026, with wall-to-wall coverage of the fight for control of Congress, polling and betting-market forecasts pointing to a Democratic wave, late-breaking campaign drama in Michigan, and election-security and legal fights over ballot counting. Secondary threads include growing private GOP frustration with Trump, a last-minute Supreme Court ruling on California ballots, and threats against lawmakers' offices.

stories.headline: Election Day arrives with control of Congress on the line
stories.summary: Americans are voting in a midterm election that will determine House and Senate control, with Trump's political capital and legislative agenda directly at stake.

stories.headline: Polls, models and betting markets converge on a Democratic 'blue tsunami'
stories.summary: Axios reports nearly every major forecaster is pointing to a Democratic rout, with Nate Silver's model giving Democrats a 95% chance of winning the House and 80% for the Senate, and Cook Political Report's upper-end scenario putting Democrats at 240 House seats; pollsters caution of possible non-response bias undercounting Republicans.

stories.headline: Haley Stevens' surprise GOP endorsement scrambles Michigan Senate race
stories.summary: Rep. Haley Stevens' late break to back Republican Mike Rogers over fellow Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has roiled the pivotal Michigan Senate race and appears to have united Democrats behind El-Sayed in its final hours.

stories.headline: Suspect charged in nationwide spree of powder-filled letters sent to lawmakers
stories.summary: Federal prosecutors charged an Oklahoma man with mailing hundreds of threatening letters containing a white powdery substance to lawmakers, election offices and media organizations in the run-up to Election Day.

stories.headline: Susan Collins' Maine office vandalized on eve of election
stories.summary: A constituent service office for Sen. Susan Collins was vandalized with graffiti overnight, the second such incident in two months as she fights a tight reelection race.

stories.headline: Supreme Court rejects Trump DOJ's bid to freeze California ballot counting
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court denied a last-ditch Trump administration request to force California to set aside ballots from suspected noncitizen voters, hours before Election Day polls opened.

stories.headline: Republicans privately blame Trump as midterm losses loom
stories.summary: Politico reports that while few GOP lawmakers criticize Trump publicly, many are venting privately about his role in the party's grim midterm outlook.

stories.headline: AOC circulates memo touting her midterm influence amid 2028 speculation
stories.summary: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez sent allies a memo highlighting her role boosting Democratic candidates this cycle, fueling chatter about a potential 2028 presidential bid.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS: no recent election-related coverage surfaced via available search access. Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian block web search, so only the provided feed items from those outlets were used.

Tech & AI.overview: Tech and AI coverage over the past day is dominated by Anthropic's IPO-related financial disclosures (surging revenue but worsening compute margins and a warning about near-term 'recursive self-improvement' capability), the fallout from Binance's record $6.3 billion North Korean hacking heist, and AI labs' efforts to safeguard the US midterm elections from disinformation. Business press is also closely tracking AI infrastructure economics, China-US chip tensions, and OpenAI's claim that ChatGPT search volume is closing in on Google's.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals worsening compute economics and RSI warning
stories.summary: Anthropic's revised S-1 filing shows revenue reaching $17 billion in Q3 but compute now consuming 58% of revenue, up from 48% the prior quarter, even as the company discloses it may be nearing 'dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI' under its own safety policy.

stories.headline: Binance says North Korean hackers used fake job interviews to pull off $6.3B crypto heist
stories.summary: Binance disclosed that suspected North Korean attackers used a fake job interview and malicious download to compromise an engineer and ultimately steal billions, a scheme cybersecurity researchers had warned about for years.

stories.headline: AI labs set up 'war rooms' to fight election disinformation ahead of US midterms
stories.summary: OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies have mobilized special teams—including Anthropic's first-ever dedicated 'war room'—to prevent their tools from being used to disrupt Tuesday's midterm elections.

stories.headline: NYT sues Brave browser over paywall blocker and AI deals
stories.summary: The New York Times filed suit accusing Brave of acting as a 'supplier, dealer, and distributor' of stolen news content through its paywall-circumvention features and AI partnerships.

stories.headline: OpenAI says ChatGPT search volume is now 20% of Google's
stories.summary: OpenAI announced that ChatGPT's search query volume now equals roughly 20 percent of Google's, with weekly active users reportedly hitting 1.2 billion after adding 200 million users in two months.

stories.headline: AI inference startup Fal doubles valuation to $16B
stories.summary: The five-year-old startup raised a $1.3 billion round led by Bessemer, doubling its valuation from $8 billion in April as it reportedly hit $800 million in annualized revenue.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike spends nearly $500M buying two AI security startups
stories.summary: CrowdStrike is acquiring Fiddler AI, which makes AI agent observability software, and Dreadnode, which automates AI security testing, as the market for securing AI agents accelerates.

stories.headline: Nvidia pushes cloud customers to scale back China business
stories.summary: Nvidia has told some cloud customers to take on less business from Chinese companies, part of a broader pattern of US chip restrictions as Huawei separately pushes customers toward black-market memory sourcing for its AI chips.

Tech & AI.gaps: Could not find search results for Platformer, Google DeepMind, or VentureBeat with clearly current (last 24-48h) lead stories; VentureBeat's most recent visible items were several days old and Platformer's site searches surfaced mostly older archive content. The Economist, FT, WSJ, Guardian, Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, and NYT were represented only via provided feed items since direct search access is blocked for several of these.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are converging on the US Senate permitting bill's likely climate impact, record third-quarter profits for Saudi Aramco, the run-up to COP31 in Antalya, and the accelerating strain data centers are putting on US utilities and grids. Utility Dive's earnings coverage and Carbon Brief's COP31 package dominate near-term attention, while Bloomberg, Canary Media and Heatmap track parallel threads on power imports, clean-energy jobs, and election-season gas prices.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco Profit Jumps Despite Pipeline and Refinery Attacks
stories.summary: State-owned Saudi Aramco reported a roughly 9% rise in third-quarter profit, helped by steady crude volumes and higher refined-product prices even after damage to pipelines and refineries.

stories.headline: New Modeling Finds Senate Permitting Bill Would Likely Cut Emissions
stories.summary: A new Rhodium Group analysis of the bipartisan permitting bill (BAAJA) finds it would likely modestly cut US emissions and electricity bills by 2040, or at worst leave emissions flat, because transmission gains offset an expanded gas pipeline buildout; a former FERC chairman writing in Utility Dive argues the bill still needs amendments to curb its riskiest provisions.

stories.headline: COP31 Nears Amid Warnings on 'Really Scary' Science
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's COP31 coverage includes the UK climate minister's call for the Antalya summit to confront alarming new science, a state-of-the-climate report projecting 2026 will tie 2024 as the warmest year on record, and an interactive mapping what different countries want from the talks.

stories.headline: Utilities Lean Into Storage and Nuclear as Data Centers Strain Grids
stories.summary: Exelon's CEO said the company plans roughly $8 billion in energy storage and transmission investment partly to address a PJM supply crunch, while Dominion reported a $137 million net income boost from rate increases and PSEG floated a 200-MW nuclear uprate to chase data-center deals, all against a backdrop of PJM scaling back its data-center backstop procurement.

stories.headline: Hydro-Quebec Forced to Import More Power After US Utility Deals
stories.summary: Hydro-Quebec is stretching a roughly C$200 billion investment plan by six years to 2041 and may need to import power in the meantime after signing major export contracts with US utilities.

stories.headline: William Nordhaus, Nobel-Winning Economist Who Shaped Climate Policy, Dies
stories.summary: The Yale economist who brought climate change into mainstream economic analysis and won a Nobel Prize for his work has died, a loss widely noted across economics and climate-policy circles.

stories.headline: Gas Prices Hit Record High on Eve of US Midterms
stories.summary: The average US gasoline price under President Trump's second term topped $3.46 a gallon as of Monday, exceeding the previous high set under Biden, with the nationwide average hitting nearly $4.17 on November 2, just as Murban crude tied to Gulf tanker attacks tumbled.

stories.headline: US Clean Energy Jobs Fell in 2025 for the First Time in Years
stories.summary: Clean-energy employment dipped during Trump's first year back in office, with Canary Media noting many more expected jobs won't materialize because of canceled clean-energy projects.

Energy.gaps: Argus Media had no searchable recent coverage found. E&E News's public site shows only outdated 2026 archive content after its move behind POLITICO Pro, so no current 24-48h items could be confirmed. Reuters, FT, WSJ, NYT and The Economist were reported only via the feed items provided, since these outlets block web search.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: China-focused outlets are dominated by Beijing's efforts to stabilize a slumping stock market and currency, alongside a fresh wave of anti-corruption prosecutions following the Communist Party's fifth plenum. Business coverage centers on mixed corporate results in China (Apple, BMW, EV makers) and continued US-China tech friction, while Hong Kong outlets track the sentencing of activist Joshua Wong and tightening party oversight of officials.

stories.headline: Beijing unveils stock buyback and liquidity measures to prop up falling market
stories.summary: China announced a package of measures including eased share-buyback rules, a third round of the central bank's swap facility, and a permanent lending program for buybacks, after a sharp October stock slide; the PBOC said the swap operations could inject over $15 billion.

stories.headline: PBOC raises forex deposit reserve requirement for first time since 2021 to cool yuan's rally
stories.summary: The People's Bank of China will raise the forex deposit reserve requirement ratio from 4% to 6% effective November 15, aiming to slow a yuan rally that has pushed the currency to its strongest level in more than four years.

stories.headline: Chinese Communist Party to tighten scrutiny of officials' assets and online activity
stories.summary: A newly released party document signals Beijing is stepping up oversight of officials, including closer monitoring of their assets and online behavior, as part of an intensified anti-corruption push following the party's fifth plenum.

stories.headline: Former Guangzhou party chief expelled and referred for prosecution on corruption charges
stories.summary: China's Communist Party expelled former Guangzhou party chief Guo Yonghang over allegations of trading favors for land deals and accepting free luxury medical care, making him the first provincial-level official referred for prosecution since the fifth plenum concluded.

stories.headline: Joshua Wong to be sentenced Thursday in second national security trial
stories.summary: A Hong Kong court has scheduled sentencing for pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong in his second national security case, which could carry up to life imprisonment.

stories.headline: Apple's Greater China revenue climbs 21% but falls short of forecasts
stories.summary: Apple's fiscal fourth-quarter Greater China revenue rose 21% year-on-year to $17.54 billion, growth that nonetheless missed market expectations of $18.75 billion.

stories.headline: BMW's China joint venture reportedly cuts about 1,800 jobs amid sales slump
stories.summary: BMW Brilliance reportedly began layoffs on November 2 affecting multiple job categories, primarily production workers, as the automaker's China sales come under pressure.

stories.headline: China accuses Philippine politicians of 'intolerable' conduct as South China Sea tensions escalate
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi accused a number of Philippine politicians of 'egregious, irrational and intolerable' conduct, urging Manila to rein in anti-China rhetoric amid continuously escalating bilateral tensions.

China.gaps: No recent distinct coverage found for Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Yicai Global, CGTN, China Daily, or Xinhua (Xinhua content appeared only as wire credits within Global Times pages); Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, WSJ and The Economist were limited to the feed items provided since they block web search.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf, Israeli and pan-Arab outlets is dominated by the fallout from Trump's surprise announcement that Washington will end military aid to Israel, closely intertwined with new U.S. strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island and fragile ceasefire diplomacy playing out on U.S. midterm election day. Saudi Aramco's strong Q3 earnings and its deepening AI push provide the main business counterweight to the geopolitical turmoil.

stories.headline: Trump says US will end $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel by end of 2026
stories.summary: Trump claimed Netanyahu personally proposed ending nearly $4 billion in annual US assistance to Israel, saying the two leaders had agreed months ago that aid would stop by December 2026, even though the formal bilateral agreement runs through 2028. Israeli finance and defense officials said they were caught off guard, and politician Gadi Eisenkot said Netanyahu 'can no longer be trusted.'

stories.headline: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as diplomacy and midterms collide
stories.summary: The US carried out limited, undeclared strikes on Iranian targets near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on the eve of US midterm elections, with Trump later confirming the attack as a 'minor' hit on an anti-aircraft facility while Iran's president warned that renewed war would benefit no one. Netanyahu was separately reported to be pushing Trump for a fresh wave of strikes after losing his parliamentary majority, while Qatar and other mediators voiced hope for a negotiated settlement.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco's Q3 profit jumps as war disrupts energy infrastructure
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco's net profit rose 34.5 percent year-on-year to $36.3 billion in the third quarter, boosted by higher revenue and a gain from selling its stake in a Malaysian refining venture, while adjusted net income climbed 9 percent to $31.2 billion despite Houthi attacks on its facilities and Hormuz disruptions. The board declared a $21.9 billion base dividend, a 3.5 percent increase, even as CEO Amin Nasser warned the conflict continues to weigh on energy security.

stories.headline: Israel warns US that Iran may be preparing chemical weapons
stories.summary: Israeli intelligence officials told American counterparts they believe Iran is rapidly advancing technology to mount chemical weapons on missiles, a claim Washington reportedly greeted with both alarm and skepticism, with some US officials viewing it as part of Netanyahu's pressure campaign to resume strikes.

stories.headline: Yemen accuses IRGC and Hezbollah of sending 21 agents to direct Houthi operations
stories.summary: Yemen's interior minister said foreign involvement in backing the Houthis has expanded beyond arms and training to directly directing military operations, naming 21 Iranian and Hezbollah operatives embedded with the rebels.

stories.headline: Israeli ex-generals help Palestinian farmers amid olive harvest settler violence
stories.summary: A group of senior Israeli ex-military officials joined Palestinian farmers in the West Bank to help harvest olives, a gesture of solidarity amid a reported upsurge in settler violence against Palestinian communities.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia leans on Aramco to bankroll AI ambitions via Humain stake
stories.summary: Aramco's 49 percent, $2.6 billion purchase of AI firm Humain is easing pressure on Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund as Riyadh uses national champions to finance new industries, with analysts saying it deepens links between the kingdom's energy, tech and finance institutions.

stories.headline: Global stocks erase losses, oil tumbles after Trump says US will end $4 billion funding to Israel

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not verify recent coverage from Ynetnews, Iran International, Al Arabiya English, Zawya or Saudi Gazette; Reuters, AP, BBC and The Economist are search-blocked so only the pre-supplied feed items (if any) were used for them.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage across the group converges on South Africa's municipal elections and the fallout from Washington stripping South Africa and Rwanda of AGOA trade privileges, alongside a wave of finance-sector reporting out of the Africa Financial Summit (AFIS) in Luanda. Business and policy outlets are also tracking Senegal's stalled IMF budget talks, Dangote's oversubscribed refinery IPO, and a widening Ebola outbreak across several African countries.

stories.headline: South Africa's municipal elections test fragmented party system
stories.summary: With a record 546 parties contesting Wednesday's vote and polls pointing to coalition governments in major cities, the key question is whether rival parties can agree on governance afterward. Africanews separately reported that service-delivery failures in Johannesburg, including weeks of water disruption, are dominating voter concerns.

stories.headline: US removes South Africa and Rwanda from AGOA trade programme
stories.summary: Washington has formally ended preferential trade access for South Africa and Rwanda under AGOA after months of diplomatic tension, a long-anticipated move. TechCabal reported the decision could hit South African startups well beyond the exporters directly covered by the programme.

stories.headline: Senegalese lawmakers reject budget, jeopardizing IMF bailout talks
stories.summary: Dakar's hopes of securing a $2.2 billion three-year IMF programme to stabilise public finances suffered a setback after parliament rejected a key budget bill.

stories.headline: Africa Financial Summit grapples with $4 trillion in idle savings
stories.summary: At the Africa Financial Summit in Luanda, policymakers and financiers are debating why Africa's highly profitable banks still extend so little credit to the private sector. TechCabal reported that AFC's CEO argued tech alone won't fix the informal economy without reliable power and transport, while the IFC outlined plans to use cash-flow data to expand lending to small businesses.

stories.headline: Dangote refinery's $1.6bn IPO draws nearly triple demand
stories.summary: Nigerian investors placed roughly $4.78 billion in orders for the Dangote refinery share sale ahead of a planned November listing, according to Africa Confidential's insider newsletter.

stories.headline: Madagascar teams with Gemcorp to raise up to $5bn for energy and mining
stories.summary: Madagascar is seeking to raise as much as $5 billion in partnership with asset manager Gemcorp Capital Management to fund energy, infrastructure and mining projects on the island, per a Bloomberg report carried by Mining Weekly.

stories.headline: Tanzania opposition leader's treason verdict looms over Samia presidency
stories.summary: Africa Confidential's insider newsletter says a verdict in opposition figure Lissu's treason case is seen as a test of President Samia's political record, arriving as Commonwealth leaders meet and victims' families press for accountability over past election violence.

Africa.gaps: No recent Africa-specific coverage could be found for Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT or WSJ, which block web search and had no relevant feed items provided; The Continent's available material was limited to older archived issues rather than the last 48 hours.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past day is dominated by the US midterm elections — with outlets dissecting how networks are covering results and what it means for Trump's relationship with the press — alongside a cluster of AI-and-publishing stories: a new cross-platform opt-out tool from major AI firms, ongoing publisher-versus-AI litigation, and simmering publisher anger at Meta's scraping terms. Entertainment-trade outlets (Variety, Deadline, THR, TheWrap) are converging on Netflix's new AI recommendation feature and the Blumhouse-Atomic Monster rebrand.

stories.headline: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Microsoft to simplify publisher opt-outs from AI scraping
stories.summary: The four AI giants announced a joint effort so publishers no longer have to block each company's crawlers individually, a significant shift in the publisher-versus-AI standoff that Press Gazette and Digiday have also been tracking this week.

stories.headline: Networks prepare marathon midterm election coverage
stories.summary: NYT reports networks are flooding viewers with options including 13 straight hours of NBC coverage and a continuous Steve Kornacki big-board livestream, as newsrooms across TV and digital gear up for Election Day.

stories.headline: Murdochs’ MAGA Math: Fox News ratings plunge as Trump's standing fades
stories.summary: Status reports that with Fox News ratings plunging and Trump's political fortunes fading, the Murdochs face a dilemma that could signal the beginning of the end of the network's MAGA-era strategy.

stories.headline: Publishers escalate legal war against AI firms: US papers sue Brave Software, Canadians sue Anthropic
stories.summary: Press Gazette's running tracker of publisher-AI litigation and licensing deals notes new lawsuits from US newspapers against Brave Software and from Canadian publishers against Anthropic.

stories.headline: Publishers furious over Meta's AI terms change but can't afford to quit Facebook
stories.summary: Digiday reports publishers are pushing back against Meta's AI scraping terms while testing how much leverage they actually have over a platform they still depend on.

stories.headline: Judge rules against 'famous man' but ITN/Guardian injunction stays pending appeal
stories.summary: A UK court ruled against an anonymous claimant who argued publication of a story about abuse of power would drive him to suicide, though the injunction blocking ITN and The Guardian's reporting remains in place pending appeal.

stories.headline: Netflix launches AI-powered 'Discover' recommendations feature on TVs
stories.summary: Netflix is rolling out an AI-branded content recommendation feature to US English-language TV subscribers as the company grapples with declining viewer engagement, according to Variety, with THR, TheWrap and Deadline also covering the launch.

stories.headline: Cavendish Press court-reporting agency closes after nearly 50 years
stories.summary: Cavendish Press's boss said publisher "greed" and low freelance rates left court reporters "facing extinction," forcing the closure of the agency.

Media.gaps: Puck, WSJ, FT and The Guardian yielded no outlet-specific media-industry items beyond what was already in the provided feed (WSJ's Netflix viewing-hours piece and FT's Binance story are economy/crypto, not strictly media-industry news); Puck's site returned only static/about-page content rather than fresh 24-48h articles.
